paper_id: K-ANMI_ A Mutual Information Based Clustering Algorithm for Categorical Data
title: K-ANMI: A Mutual Information Based Clustering Algorithm for Categorical Data
motivation: Categorical data clustering lacks efficient algorithms; existing ensemble approaches rely on intuitive heuristics that cannot guarantee reasonable solutions.
problem_framing: Define categorical clustering as optimization problem maximizing ANMI (Average Normalized Mutual Information) borrowed from cluster ensemble literature.
key_insight: Treating each attribute's value partition as a clustering result allows reformulating categorical clustering as a cluster ensemble consensus problem.
method_signature: k-means style iterative algorithm directly optimizing ANMI objective using histogram-based data structures for scalability.
evaluation_criteria: Clustering accuracy (r = sum of a_i / n) compared against Squeezer, GAClust, and ccdByEnsemble on UCI datasets.
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: Algorithm terminates at local optimum; worst-case complexity O(I*n*k²*r*p²) requires practical assumptions on small p.
evidence_for_taste: intuitive heuristics rather than from vantage point
can't guarantee to find a reasonable solution
direct optimization strategy utilized in k-ANMI is more desirable
algorithm is capable of handing large categorical datasets
thinking_moves: 把直观启发式方法替换为直接优化目标函数
借用cluster ensemble框架中的ANMI作为聚类准则
用直方图/哈希表实现避免访问原始数据集
先分析理论复杂度再验证实际线性可扩展性
extraction_notes: Authors reference their own ccdByEnsemble work as baseline to beat; this demonstrates internal motivation to improve prior approach. Venue inferred as data mining conference but arxiv version doesn't specify.
